content.title: II. Anticoagulant drugs

table_entries.initial_treatment: i.v. bolus 70–100 U/kg followed by i.v. infusion titrated to achieve an aPTT of 60–80 s.
table_entries.during_PCI: 70–100 U/kg i.v. bolus or according to ACT in case of UFH pre-treatment.
table_entries.notes: UFH = unfractionated heparin; ACT = activated clotting time; aPTT = activated partial thromboplastin time.

table_entries.initial_treatment: For treatment of ACS: 1 mg/kg b.i.d. subcutaneously for a minimum of 2 days and continued until clinical stabilization. If CrCl <30 mL/min (by Cockcroft–Gault), reduce dosage to 1 mg/kg o.d.
table_entries.during_PCI: If last dose given <8 h before balloon inflation, no additional dosing is needed. If last s.c. administration >8 h before balloon inflation, administer i.v. bolus of 0.3 mg/kg enoxaparin sodium.
table_entries.notes: CrCl = creatinine clearance; b.i.d. = twice a day; o.d. = once a day; Cockcroft–Gault equation referenced for renal dosing.

table_entries.during_PPCI: 0.75 mg/kg i.v. bolus followed by i.v. infusion of 1.75 mg/kg/h for 4 h after the procedure.
table_entries.dose_adjustment: In patients with CrCl <30 mL/min (by Cockcroft–Gault), maintenance infusion should be reduced to 1 mg/kg/h.
table_entries.notes: PPCI = primary percutaneous coronary intervention; CrCl and Cockcroft–Gault referenced for renal dosing.

table_entries.during_PCI: A single bolus of UFH is recommended during PCI.
table_entries.notes: UFH recommended as single bolus during PCI when fondaparinux is used.

additional_section.title: I. Antiplatelet drugs (excerpt)
additional_section.Aspirin: LD of 150–300 mg orally or 75–250 mg i.v. if oral ingestion not possible, followed by oral MD of 75–100 mg o.d.; no specific dose adjustment in CKD patients.
